Sure! Those numbers are already a pair of geographic coordinates (latitude = 37.4224764, longitude = ‑122.0842499). If you want to verify them or look up what’s at that spot, you can use the **Google Maps Geocoding API** to perform a *reverse‑geocode* query.

Below is a quick example of how you would call the API (you’ll need a valid API key):

```http
GET https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?latlng=37.4224764,-122.0842499&key=YOUR_API_KEY
```

If you run that request, the JSON response will contain an `address_components` array that describes the place. For the coordinates you supplied, the response looks something like this (truncated for brevity):

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "address_components": [
        { "long_name": "1600", "short_name": "1600", "types": ["street_number"] },
        { "long_name": "Amphitheatre Parkway", "short_name": "Amphitheatre Pkwy", "types": ["route"] },
        { "long_name": "Mountain View", "short_name": "Mountain View", "types": ["locality", "political"] },
        { "long_name": "Santa Clara County", "short_name": "Santa Clara County", "types": ["administrative_area_level_2", "political"] },
        { "long_name": "California", "short_name": "CA", "types": ["administrative_area_level_1", "political"] },
        { "long_name": "United States", "short_name": "US", "types": ["country", "political"] },
        { "long_name": "94043", "short_name": "94043", "types": ["postal_code"] }
      ],
      "formatted_address": "1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA",
      "geometry": {
        "location": { "lat": 37.4224764, "lng": -122.0842499 },
        ...
      },
      ...
    }
  ],
  "status": "OK"
}
```

So the coordinates you gave point to the Googleplex at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. If you’d like to see the full response or test it yourself, just replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with your own key and hit the URL.
